title: C Layout and Pointer Arithmetic
goal: Understand C memory layout guarantees and raw pointer arithmetic.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Foreign Function Interface

sections.text: Rust reorders struct fields by default to optimize alignment. C compilers do not.

sections.caption: The repr(C) attribute guarantees field order matches C.

sections.text: Raw pointer arithmetic with `ptr.add(n)` advances by `n` elements, not `n` bytes.

sections.caption: add(1) steps forward by one u32 (4 bytes).

sections.text: To step forward in raw byte counts, cast the pointer to `*const u8` first.

sections.code:
let byte_ptr = ptr as *const u8;
let b = unsafe { *byte_ptr.add(4) };
sections.caption: Casting to u8 pointer allows byte-level stepping.

explanation: Understand C memory layout guarantees and raw pointer arithmetic.
